    Weighted marginal risks and contrasts

    Source: R/causal-weighting.R
    epi_weighted_effect.Rd

    Computes separately normalized (Hájek) weighted risks for the exposed and unexposed groups, their difference, and their ratio. Effective sample sizes are (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) within each group. With bootstrap > 0, records are resampled with their supplied weights held fixed and percentile intervals are returned for the risk difference and ratio. Holding estimated propensity weights fixed ignores their estimation; for inverse-probability weights this usually makes intervals conservative. Use epi_ipw() to re-estimate the propensity model in every resample. This function does not test covariate balance or establish a causal interpretation.

    Usage

    epi_weighted_effect(
  .data,
  exposure,
  outcome,
  weights,
  bootstrap = 0L,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame of individual records.

    exposure

    Binary 0/1 exposure column.

    outcome

    Binary 0/1 outcome column.

    weights

    Non-negative numeric weights, with a positive total in each exposure group. Zero weights are allowed.

    bootstrap

    Number of individual bootstrap resamples: 0 (no intervals) or an integer from 100 to 2000.

    conf_level

    Confidence level strictly between zero and one.

    Value

    A one-row tibble with group risks, risk difference, risk ratio, effective sample sizes and original sample size, plus percentile limits for the difference and ratio when bootstrapping. An undefined ratio is NA.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(e = c(0, 0, 1, 1), y = c(0, 1, 1, 1), w = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
epi_weighted_effect(d, e, y, w)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   risk_unexposed risk_exposed risk_difference risk_ratio ess_unexposed
#>            <dbl>        <dbl>           <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1            0.5            1             0.5          2             2
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: ess_exposed <dbl>, n <int>
